passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. For the discussion of the financial condition and results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, refer to "Part II—Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 filed with the SEC on February 6, 2025, which is incorporated herein by reference. Overview Our Business Hilton is one of the largest global hospitality companies, with 9,158 properties comprising 1,351,351 rooms in 143 countries and territories as of December 31, 2025. Our premier brand portfolio includes luxury, lifestyle, full service, focused service and all-suites hotel brands, as well as timeshare brands. As of December 31, 2025, we had 243 million members in our award-winning guest loyalty program, Hilton Honors, an increase of 15 percent from December 31, 2024. Segments and Regions We analyze our operations and business by both operating segments and geographic regions. Our operations consist of two reportable segments that are based on similar products and services: (i) management and franchise and (ii) ownership. The management and franchise segment provides services, including hotel management and licensing of our IP and/or the use of our booking channels and related programs. Revenues from this segment include: (i) management and franchise fees charged to third-party hotel owners; (ii) licensing fees from our strategic partners, including co-branded credit card providers and strategic partner hotels, and HGV; and (iii) fees for managing the hotels in our ownership segment. As a manager of hotels, we typically are responsible for supervising or operating the hotel in exchange for management fees. As a franchisor of hotels, we charge franchise fees in exchange for the use of one of our brand names and/or related commercial services, such as our reservations system, marketing and information technology services, while a third party manages or operates such franchised hotels. The ownership segment primarily derives revenues from nightly hotel room sales, food and beverage sales and other services at our consolidated hotels. We conduct business in three distinct geographic regions: (i) the Americas; (ii) Europe, Middle East and Africa ("EMEA"); and (iii) Asia Pacific. The Americas region includes North America, South America and Central America, including all Caribbean nations. Although the U.S., which represented 64 percent of our system-wide hotel rooms as of December 31, 2025, is included in the Americas region, it is often analyzed separately and apart from the Americas region and, as such, it is presented separately within our hotel operating statistics in "—Results of Operations." passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: In addition to the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, the following risk factors should be considered carefully in evaluating our company and our business. Risks Related to Our Industry We are subject to the business, financial and operating risks inherent to the hospitality industry, any of which could reduce our revenues and limit opportunities for growth. Our business is subject to a number of business, financial and operating risks inherent to the hospitality industry, including: • significant competition from multiple hospitality providers in all parts of the world; • changes in the supply and demand for hotel services, including rooms, food and beverage and other products and services; • the financial condition of and relationships with third-party property owners, developers and joint venture and strategic partners, including the risk that owners or strategic partners may terminate or fail to comply with our management, franchise, joint venture or strategic partner contracts; • decreases in the frequency of business travel that may result from alternatives to in-person meetings, including virtual meetings hosted online or over private teleconferencing networks; • decreases in the availability and/or increases in the cost of capital necessary for us and third-party hotel owners to fund investments, capital expenditures and service debt obligations; • increases in operating costs, including employee compensation and benefits, energy, insurance, food and beverage and other supplies; • significant increases in cost for health care coverage for employees and potential government regulation with respect to health care coverage; • increases in costs due to inflation or other factors that may not be fully offset by increases in revenues in our business, as well as increases in overall consumer prices, including the prices of our offerings, due to inflation, which could weaken consumer demand for travel and the other products we offer and adversely affect our revenues; • changes in taxes, tariffs and governmental regulations that affect the cost of supplies to hotels or influence or set wages, prices, interest rates or construction and maintenance procedures and costs; • the costs and administrative burdens associated with complying with applicable laws and regulations; • the costs or desirability of complying with local practices and customs; • shortages of labor or labor disruptions; • the ability of third-party internet and other travel intermediaries who sell our hotel rooms to guests to attract and retain customers, including with the aid of AI, which may adversely affect our ability to sell rooms directly; • the quality of services provided by franchisees, as well as their ability to comply with relevant regulations and contractual requirements relating to a variety of issues including the environment, human rights and labor; credit_strengths.text: Hilton's asset-light management and franchise model generates high-margin fee streams, with operating margin well above the sector median and revenue growing steadily across the disclosed annual trend. This supports resilient cash generation and reduces exposure to hotel ownership volatility.

Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure, producing substantial free cash flow that exceeds reported interest expense. This internally generated liquidity provides a buffer against cyclical hospitality demand and supports the current debt load.

key_risks.text: The risk factors highlight dependence on third-party hotel owners and strategic partners, including potential contract termination or non-compliance. Such events could disrupt fee streams and impair cash flow, a material vulnerability given the franchise-heavy revenue base.

The debt note shows a large senior secured term loan maturing in the medium term and a cluster of senior notes due thereafter, with significant refinancing needs. The revolving facility was undrawn but borrowed and repaid during the year, indicating reliance on capital markets access.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is adequate but sits below the sector median, reflecting the heavy debt load. Operating income covers interest expense multiple times, yet the margin of safety is thinner than peers, leaving less room for earnings volatility.

Free cash flow to debt is modest and below sector norms, while the current ratio is weak, indicating limited near-term liquidity relative to liabilities. However, substantial undrawn revolver capacity and consistent operating cash flow mitigate immediate refinancing risk.

overall_credit_view.text: Leverage is elevated and sits well above the sector median, with net leverage near the threshold for a more aggressive profile. The indicative financial risk profile is aggressive, and the Altman Z-score falls in the distress zone, signalling limited headroom for further debt-funded shareholder returns.

Shareholder distributions, particularly buybacks, absorb most free cash flow, constraining deleveraging. While the asset-light model and growing fee revenue support credit quality, the combination of high leverage, weak current ratio and refinancing needs warrants a cautious outlook.

credit_strengths.text: 希爾頓的輕資產管理及特許經營模式產生高利潤率的費用收入流，其營運利潤率遠高於行業中位數，且收入在披露的年度趨勢中穩步增長。這支持了具韌性的現金產生能力，並減低了對酒店擁有權波動的曝險。
營運現金流足以覆蓋資本開支，產生超過報告利息支出的可觀自由現金流。此內部產生的流動性為週期性酒店需求提供了緩衝，並支持當前的債務負擔。

key_risks.text: 風險因素突顯了對第三方酒店擁有人及策略夥伴的依賴，包括潛在的合約終止或不合規。此類事件可能中斷費用收入流並損害現金流，鑑於以特許經營為主的收入基礎，這是一項重大脆弱性。
債務票據顯示一筆大額高級抵押定期貸款於中期到期，以及隨後到期的一批高級票據，存在重大的再融資需求。循環信貸額度未動用，但在年內曾借入並償還，顯示依賴資本市場准入。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率充足，但低於行業中位數，反映沉重的債務負擔。營運收入覆蓋利息支出數倍，然而安全邊際較同業為薄，為盈利波動留下的空間較少。
自由現金流對債務比率適度且低於行業常規，而流動比率疲弱，顯示相對於負債，近期流動性有限。然而，大量未動用的循環信貸額度及穩定的營運現金流緩解了即時再融資風險。

overall_credit_view.text: 槓桿高企且遠高於行業中位數，淨槓桿接近更進取狀況的門檻。指示性財務風險狀況為進取，而Altman Z-score落入困境區域，預示進一步以債務融資的股東回報空間有限。
股東分派，尤其是回購，吸收了大部分自由現金流，限制了去槓桿。儘管輕資產模式及增長的費用收入支持信貸質量，高槓桿、疲弱流動比率及再融資需求的組合值得審慎展望。
